speaker: jacqueline_field
text: The shop is shut. Come up. There is lamb, and the first peas, and you will not talk of paper until you have eaten.

speaker: richard_field
text: Sit, Will. I live like a printer who keeps his doors shut on a Sunday. Here is thy bundle, back.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I came to be angry at this table, as thou bidst me on Thursday. I am hungry first.

speaker: richard_field
text: Thou mayest be both. I read it with the door shut. I have a verdict, and it is in two parts.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Give me the first, and carve while thou sayest it.

speaker: richard_field
text: It is wanton.

speaker: jacqueline_field
text: He has a second part. Let him finish before you defend it.

speaker: richard_field
text: It is also the best-made thing I have read that was not in Latin. Give me the copy, and I will print it as it should be printed.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: The copy is Garnish's, and the company's. I have not a leaf of it that is mine to hand thee.

speaker: richard_field
text: Then one day a Millington will have it from a hired man for forty pence.

speaker: jacqueline_field
text: He is right, and you are right, and it will happen.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Forty pence is a hired man's supper and a week's regret. The book stays with Garnish.

speaker: richard_field
text: I told thee the trade on Thursday. The man's who entered it. Honest presswork on a dishonest copy, and the octavo is already in the world.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I was curious whose it was. Thou answeredst. That curiosity is spent.

speaker: richard_field
text: And the Holinshed. The gap is still on my shelf. I said Sunday.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Sunday. Not the Holinshed.

speaker: jacqueline_field
text: Then the king is not coming to the table either. Eat the peas.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: The king is not finished. That is all I will say of him.

speaker: richard_field
text: The peas, then. And after them, home. They talk of thin corn, and whether the bailiff will stint the maltsters. I have it as talk, not as a letter that decides it.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I have no newer word than Thursday. Susanna is twelve. The twins are ten. The letter went, and Hobbins had nothing to put in my hand.

speaker: jacqueline_field
text: Twelve is a great age for a letter. We will not improve it from Blackfriars.

speaker: jacqueline_field
text: Are the streets quiet by Bishopsgate?

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Quiet enough.

speaker: richard_field
text: Quiet enough is a short answer. I will not ask thee twice.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Then thou hast the whole of it. The lamb is very good.

speaker: jacqueline_field
text: We will talk of the corn, and not of the streets. You have said quiet enough. Let it stand.

speaker: richard_field
text: Come when thou hast a poem. I can wait for a poem. I cannot make a company give me its book.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I will come when I have one. Not with the chronicle, and not with the comedy.

speaker: jacqueline_field
text: Good. That is a dinner. Take the last of the peas, and go while the light holds.
